text.title: User Research at Scale Failure Modes
text.summary: Antipatterns observed in real deployments of User Research at Scale. Each ties a symptom to a root cause and a concrete fix. Folds in the former gotchas file: Known AI failure modes in scaled research: sentiment accuracy, hallucination risks, cost traps, privacy requirements, and cross-platform normalization.

antipattern.symptom: Weekly codes grew from 80 to 240 in 3 weeks; comparability lost. Letting the theme-coder invent codes when the codebook is unclear rather than using the proposed_codes overflow channel.
antipattern.root-cause: Auto-extension without HITL. Invented codes contaminate the taxonomy and produce theme drift across batches. Strict allow-list enforcement with a separate proposed_codes channel keeps the codebook clean.
antipattern.fix: Freeze book; route novelty to proposed_codes; require HITL accept before merge.
Enforce evidence_count>=50, session_count>=10, segment_count>=2 at publish.
Route through ZDR-eligible endpoints; lint outbound calls.

antipattern.symptom: Same note appears 3x in Dovetail after retries.
antipattern.fix: Hash (source_url + date) as idempotency key; reject duplicates.

antipattern.symptom: Running sentiment analysis on non-English transcripts without routing by language.
antipattern.root-cause: Sentiment models miss sarcasm, code-switching, and culture-specific affect in non-English text. Polarity flips on negation in low-resource languages without language-aware routing.
antipattern.fix: Detect language in transcript-cleaner; route non-English sessions to a language-specific model or translation step before sentiment scoring.

antipattern.symptom: Agents quietly dropping non-English sessions when the prompt does not explicitly handle them.
antipattern.root-cause: Silently dropping sessions produces a biased corpus. Assert language coverage in tests and route non-English sessions to a translation step before coding.
antipattern.fix: Count sessions per language in and out of every stage; a mismatch fails the batch.

antipattern.symptom: Hallucinating participant IDs in the report when citing quotes.
antipattern.root-cause: Agents invent participant IDs that do not exist in the corpus. Require verbatim span offsets (start_char, end_char) tied to a specific session file, not paraphrases.
antipattern.fix: Every cited quote carries session file + span offsets; the publish gate resolves each one against the corpus.

antipattern.symptom: Re-running coding on the same transcript without caching, burning 10x tokens.
antipattern.root-cause: Hash the transcript content and cache the coded output. Skip transcripts that already have a cached result. Uncached re-runs are pure waste.
antipattern.fix: `templates/code-batch.sh` dedupes on content hash; see rule prompt-cache-codebook for the codebook side.

antipattern.symptom: Feeding full transcript bundles > 200k tokens into a long-context model without chunking.
antipattern.root-cause: Long-context models silently truncate at token boundaries. Chunk at session boundaries with overlap and verify completeness before synthesis.
antipattern.fix: Chunk at session boundaries with overlap; assert every session id appears in the synthesis input before the Opus call.

antipattern.symptom: Pattern-analyst over-indexing on the first segment in the prompt.
antipattern.root-cause: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily. Randomize segment order across runs and compare findings to detect position bias.
antipattern.fix: Run pattern-analyst twice with shuffled segment order; findings that survive both orders pass.

antipattern.symptom: Mixing timestamp formats from different platforms (Maze milliseconds, UserTesting ISO, Otter seconds) without normalization.
antipattern.root-cause: Mixed timestamps break quote offset matching and prevent cross-platform de-duplication. Normalize in the transcript-cleaner stage before any downstream use.
antipattern.fix: transcript-cleaner converts every timestamp to ISO 8601 with milliseconds before emitting clean VTT/JSON.
